Event: `d39a9b701d2819686edb12196ebd5a22` · 2026-09-24T21:38:29Z

> Red-team code review of b4bad072e (K5 5/8), in a scratch worktree (now removed). I ran rv64 boot cases with the main tree's RustSBI prototyper and planted bugs, reverting each. 6901def60 was ignored.
> 
> VERDICT: OK with notes on the code. The kernel wiring does what the model and redoubt-stride do, and accounting at the trap boundary is complete by reading. But the tests don't back that up yet: planted bugs in two of the new boot cases' own target rules survived. T1-T3 must be fixed before K5 merges. D1 is a design question for the orchestrator.
> 
> VERIFIED BY READING (kernel = crate = model):
> - Rank key (pass, tie, id), the floor, and wakes at max(own, floor) with descending-id front counters: the kernel calls redoubt-stride's Queue directly.
> - min 1 tick at every deschedule (sched.rs deschedule .max(1)); the exact remainder, via the crate.
> - Entry e stored in the frame words (W_SCHED+2..3).
> - The lift = crate::lift, with w_parent after the return.
> - Fold at the old weight: before_weight_change settles cur and closes its billing, then carve, then reweigh; on the budget_create failure path too.
> - Return order: the top's weight returns at mark_dying (settle, return, reweigh), children's at their lift, and pages at destroy_marked with the weight flag off. Carve refusal via holds_process; process_created refuses free weight 0.
> - One cosmetic divergence: the kernel requeues on every budget change (q.deschedule(.., true)) and lets the same entry's reconcile drop a budget that isn't runnable, so the back counter also counts blocks. The order is identical (clauses 1-4 hold, and the floor comes out the same), but a differential on the real wiring would flag counter values. See T3.
> - Accounting: from_user runs first on every SPP=User trap. leave() sits in both sret sites (resume and return_registers) and handles PID 1. A legacy direct switch or a callback is a budget change in leave, so the old budget is folded and requeued and the slice continues. Idle is stop_billing; kmain's expiry walk is paused billing.
> - Billing: per-item expiry, a deadline's destroy billed to its top before the lift, IRQs to the device owner, a syscall to its caller. Small deviation: kmain's pick after a deschedule is billed to the descheduled budget, where the plan said kernel. It is O(64) and bounded; state it.
> - Preemption only at slice end (timer from U, not in a callback) or a budget deadline (preempt at entry, sepc untouched, so the trap is retaken). A timeout never preempts. do_yield no longer panics without a SwitchTo caller.
> 
> PLANTED BUGS (rv64, reverted):
> - stride weight = limit: sched-carve-inflation FAILS (victim 397). Caught.
> - wake without the floor: sched-idle-gap FAILS (B 10/1000). Caught.
> - lift by max (the crate's lift reverted to v2's max): sched-budget-churn PASSES. Not caught.
> - exit-path accounting dropped (no from_user on ThreadExit/ProcessExit ecalls or faults): sched-exit-churn PASSES (victim 494). Not caught.
> - a timeout wake preempts: sched-sleep-gaming, sched-timer-flood and sched-share all PASS. No boot case covers it at commit 5.
> - no min-1 tick: sched-sleep-gaming PASSES (expected; hard to produce a 0-tick run under icount).
> 
> T1 (P2, merge-gating) sched-exit-churn doesn't exercise the path it exists for (review-1 P1-1). ChurnChild spins and then does rd::send (its report) before process_exit or the fault, and the thread-churn worker likewise reports before thread_exit. That send charges the whole spin, so the exit or fault ends a microsecond-long run. Restructure so the spin ends directly in the exit, fault or thread_exit: report beforehand, write the count to shared memory the parent reads, or let the parent measure the victim alone. Then show the planted 'no accounting on exit' bug fails it.
> 
> T2 (P2, merge-gating) sched-budget-churn has no sensitivity. In every variant the attacker subtree gets 0-21 of 1000 (logs: victim 950/498/978/950): spawning and R10 (~21 ms of virtual time per destroy) cost the attacker more than any churn could gain, so even the M1 max-lift passes. The kernel's lift wiring (the weights and floor sched::destroy passes to q.destroy) is therefore untested at boot. Either redesign it so an honest spinner and the attacker are comparable (children spawned once and parked, with churn only of budgets whose work is cheap), or state that the case can't be sensitive and cover the wiring with T3 plus the sched-trace oracle (commit 6: assert each lift's parent pass delta). Show the max-lift plant failing whichever check you choose.
> 
> T3 (P2, merge-gating; review-1 P2-4 still open) The differential still drives a test harness, not the kernel's sched.rs wiring. It has also now diverged from the kernel's behaviour (requeue-then-reconcile, billing folds). Factor the wiring (leave, deschedule, create, destroy, reweigh) into code the differential can drive with a fake Budgets, or reproduce the kernel's call sequence exactly, and compare order-relevant state.
> 
> T4 (P3) Nothing at boot covers 'a timeout never preempts' (only the model's sched_contracts). Commit 6's sched-ties oracle should assert no pick while a thread runs mid-slice, or add a timeouts sub-case: a sleeper waking mid-slice first runs no earlier than the spinner's slice end.
> 
> D1 (P2, design, for the orchestrator) The shell variant deviates from plan s10/(k) because of an over-penalty the rules create.
> The plan's shell carves c = a-1 (99 of 100) and runs ~1 ms commands. The case uses weight 50 with no command run, and its own comment says 99 'would make that window cost a hundred times over': the parent's syscall and spinner time while carved away is charged at free weight 1, and nothing scales it back when the weight returns (pass leads are not rescaled on a weight change).
> Related, by reading, in both kernel and model: at destroy, W = (pass - max(e,f)) x w_child uses the child's free weight at destroy (its limit, once its children have returned). If it ran with most of its weight carved away, its lead (in small-weight pass units) is lifted inflated by limit/free_then.
> Both effects only over-charge, so there is no gaming, but an honest parent that carves most of its weight to short-lived children is starved well past its share.
> Options:
> (a) Accept and document it ('a budget running while carved down pays at what it kept, and that debt is not rescaled when the weight returns'), and add the (k)-faithful variant back with an explicit, justified tolerance.
> (b) Rescale a budget's lead above max(e, f) on a weight increase (lead x w_old / w_new, remainder carried): work-conserving, and it makes the lift's lead x w_child consistent.
> This is an owner-decision-7 refinement, so the orchestrator's call; either way, restore the plan's (k) shape in the boot case.
> 
> Still open from earlier reviews (the new implementer will fold these in first): review-2 P1-1 (the ReturnToParent deferral) and the review-1 fixups.
